Sign-in fails with 'Kunne ikke starte Apple-innlogging (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED)' and there is no fallback/skip — no agenda, header masthead, events, or 'Dette dekker vi' section render at all. The product's core promise (a calm scannable agenda) is completely invisible.
Same as 375px: only the Apple sign-in card and AUTHENTICATION_FAILED error are visible; no dashboard content renders.

Same as smaller widths: only the Apple sign-in card and AUTHENTICATION_FAILED error are visible; no dashboard content renders. Additionally, at all three widths the #apple-sign-in-button area itself renders empty (CloudKit's own Sign-in-with-Apple control never appears) — once setUpAuth() fails, there is no visible interactive control to retry, only text instructing to reload the page or open DevTools.

notes: This is an unchanged repeat of the 2026-07-21/22 finding (see ui-fix-log.json, checked 2026-07-22): the gate is a deliberate owner decision (commit f905fc70a, documented inline in index.html:45-49) — body.gated hides all content until Sign in with Apple succeeds. Confirmed via git log that no commit has touched index.html, icloud-sync.js, icloud-config.js, or the .auth-gate CSS since that run, so nothing has changed here in ~6 days. ui-fix previously and correctly declined to touch it as out-of-mandate (reversing an explicit owner decision).

Could not assess ANY of the correctness/layout checklist (match name truncation, streaming channel/foreign-broadcaster check, times, flags/crests, must-see accent, header/footer) at any width — everything behind the auth gate is unreachable without a successful Apple sign-in, and this screenshot harness has no network path to Apple's CloudKit web services.
The gate screen itself (wordmark, lead copy, error text) remains well laid out at all three widths: no overflow, no clipping, no truncation, calm and centered — same visual quality as prior runs.

Flagging as high again (not escalating further) purely because it means visual QA cannot verify the actual product at all, run after run, in this offline harness. A human should confirm whether real signed-in users in production see the dashboard fine (this may be purely an artifact of the no-network screenshot environment) and whether the empty sign-in-button-on-failure state (medium finding above) also occurs for real users whose CloudKit auth fails (e.g. Safari private browsing / blocked third-party cookies), since that would be a genuine dead end with no retry control.
